items.gist: Argues that mala cannot truly obstruct jñatva and kartṛtva; any covering would imply destruction of form or mere nominal concealment.
Questions what obstructs mala's power and examines Īśvara's will, karma equality, and the timing of conflicting karmas.
Raises problems about life-span, bodily death, and whether Śaṃkara obstructs mala at a particular time.
Discusses beginningless enjoyment and karma, arguing that variety cannot be explained by mere beginninglessness or Īśvara's will.
Connects karma to māyā's operation and concludes that the standard bondage-liberation sequence is incoherent.
Examines opposing karmas, their mutual obstruction, and rejects a simple śaktipāta-based account of liberation.
Rejects proposed conditions and dependencies for śaktipāta, finding them inconsistent or inapplicable.
Presents the medicine of the āgama: Śiva freely conceals his own nature and binds himself through karma.
Explains Śiva's tirodhāna through mala and karma, while mala itself arises from differentiated desire.
Concludes that pure self-luminous Śiva is the cause; bhakti and karma differ for enjoyment versus liberation.
